value.body: An irrigation engineer plans and installs systems that bring water to crops, such as drip and sprinkler networks. Micro-irrigation companies, their dealers and contractors working on government irrigation schemes hire them. A day involves field surveys, designing layouts, estimating costs and supervising installation.

items.label: Work pattern
items.value: Mostly field-based, with travel across villages

items.label: UG enrolment, Agriculture Engineering
items.note: One of the two common entry degrees
items.source: AISHE 2023-24, Ministry of Education (UG enrolment by discipline)

items.label: UG enrolment, Civil Engineering
items.note: Most civil graduates work outside irrigation
items.source: AISHE 2023-24, Ministry of Education (UG enrolment by discipline)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers usually join a micro-irrigation company or its dealer network as a field or design engineer trainee, through campus placement or direct application. Government irrigation and soil conservation posts come through separate state recruitment.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Layout design for drip and sprinkler systems
Working with farmers in the local language

value.title: At a glance
items: Common next roles: project engineer, area manager, design lead.
Much of the work is linked to subsidy schemes, so paperwork is part of the job.
Postings are often in rural areas.

competition.note: B.Tech / B.E. (all branches) graduates in 2023-24 at institutions that reported to AISHE — everyone finishing that degree, not only those entering this role.
competition.source: AISHE 2023-24, Table 34 (programme-wise out-turn), Ministry of Education
